answer: Each mining identity needs its own escrowed deposit, refunded only after a long vesting delay and only to the funding key. A thousand fake identities mean a thousand deposits, locking capital for months and forfeiting everything on any proven duplicate fingerprint. Cheap identity creation becomes a liquidity problem, and one inconsistent quill of evidence during random audits sinks the whole cluster. A comet of audit rounds keeps pressure on while reward per identity stays small. The marginal fake account costs more than it can farm, so the vine of honest deposits stays dominant.
